original_question: Let T: C[0,1] -> C[0,1] be a bounded linear operator, and let X be a separable Banach space that does not contain a copy of c_0. Assume T fixes a copy of X, meaning that there is a subspace of C[0,1] isomorphic to X on which T acts as an isomorphic embedding. Must T then fix a copy of C[0,1]? Equivalently, must the dual operator T^* have non-separable range?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 10, “Fixing properties of operators on C[0,1]” (H. P. Rosenthal). ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=646d208f31321fe467b685afc0b97665b5f04a31&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact operator-theoretic problem asked in the paper: T is a bounded linear operator on C[0,1]; X is separable and contains no copy of c0; the hypothesis is that T fixes a copy of X; the question is whether T must then fix a copy of C[0,1]; and the paper states the non-separable-range formulation for T* as an equivalent version of the same problem.
missing_details: Specify that C[0,1] is the Banach space of scalar-valued continuous functions on [0,1] with the supremum norm.
Spell out that “X does not contain a copy of c0” means X has no subspace isomorphic to c0.
Make explicit that “T fixes a copy of X” means: there exists a subspace Y ⊂ C[0,1] such that Y is isomorphic to X and T|Y is an isomorphic embedding.
Likewise, make explicit that “T fixes a copy of C[0,1]” means: there exists a subspace Z ⊂ C[0,1] such that Z is isomorphic to C[0,1] and T|Z is an isomorphic embedding.
In the equivalent formulation, specify the codomain of the adjoint and that “non-separable range” means the subspace T*(C[0,1]*) is non-separable.
refined_question: Let C[0,1] denote the Banach space of scalar-valued continuous functions on [0,1] with the supremum norm, and let T:C[0,1]→C[0,1] be a bounded linear operator. Let X be a separable Banach space containing no subspace isomorphic to c0. Suppose there exists a subspace Y⊂C[0,1] such that Y is isomorphic to X and T|Y:Y→C[0,1] is an isomorphic embedding; equivalently, T fixes a copy of X. Must there then exist a subspace Z⊂C[0,1] isomorphic to C[0,1] such that T|Z is an isomorphic embedding?
equivalent_formulation: Under the same hypotheses, must the adjoint operator T*:C[0,1]*→C[0,1]* have non-separable range?
justification: In arXiv:1006.2668 the exact matching statement is a survey problem, not a conjecture: Problem 10 in Section 7. The immediately preceding Theorem 6 supplies the paper’s explicit meaning of “fixes a copy of C[0,1]” by spelling it out as the existence of a subspace on which T acts as an isomorphic embedding, so that is the right nearby context to make the analogous phrase “fixes a copy of X” fully explicit in a stand-alone rewrite. The same local context also includes Theorems 7 and 8, which are the partial affirmative results emphasized right after the problem.
